answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a scarce opal token: only a fixed number are minted per epoch, and an agent must win one at open auction by locking POA, the price set by the marginal bid. To forge a thousand fake identities, a farm must win a thousand tokens at a clearing price that rises with every extra bid it places, and each token's locked stake is slashed if its identity is caught attesting fraud. Cost per fake identity grows with scale instead of staying flat, and no bulk discount exists.
